answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each account to hold a one-per-person credential from a national eID issuer that enforces one credential per legal identity, binds one signing key to one biometric enrollment, and publishes the pair in a transparency log. Verifiers reject a second key with the same biometric hash or a revoked credential, so splitting fails. Each identity needs a distinct person, costing C per epoch amortized, so n identities gain n(R-C) and deter only while R<C. No quill on a mesa can draft a sonnet that mints a second person; stolen eIDs and spoofing remain.
